name: com.tributepaper/tributepaper
title: Tribute Paper
description: Funeral program and memorial card designs, obituary and eulogy help, readings and funeral planning.

tools.name: search_designs
tools.description: Search Tribute Paper's designs for funeral programs, order of service booklets, memorial and celebration of life cards, homegoing programs, Catholic funeral Mass booklets, anniversaries, headstone unveilings, death announcements, thank-you cards and pet memorials. Understands everyday words from the US, UK, Canada and Australia ("order of service", "homegoing", "year's mind") and small typos. Filter by kind of service, faith or tradition, style, color, or designs with a photo. Returns each design's name, kind, a short description and its page link. Every design comes in every size, including a folded program booklet. get_design gives one design's full details.

query.description: What the family is looking for, in their words, e.g. "catholic funeral mass booklet", "celebration of life with photo", "order of service blue". Leave out to list popular designs.

category.description: Only designs of this kind: funeral-service (Funeral Service), memorial-service (Memorial Service), celebration-of-life (Celebration of Life), homegoing-service (Homegoing Service), funeral-mass (Catholic Funeral Mass), graveside-service (Graveside Service), military-funeral (Military Funeral), first-anniversary (First Anniversary), memorial-mass (Anniversary Mass), headstone-unveiling (Headstone Unveiling), heavenly-birthday (Birthday in Heaven), ashes-scattering (Scattering of Ashes), forty-day-memorial (Forty-Day Memorial), death-announcement (Death Announcement), funeral-thank-you (Funeral Thank-You), pet-memorial (Pet Memorial).

faith.description: Only designs made for this faith or tradition: any (Non-religious / any), christian (Christian), jewish (Jewish), muslim (Muslim), hindu (Hindu), sikh (Sikh), buddhist (Buddhist), chinese (Chinese).

has_photo.description: true: only designs with a place for a photo of the person.

limit.description: How many results to return (1 to 20, default 8).

tools.name: get_design
tools.description: Details of one Tribute Paper design by its slug (from search_designs): what it is for, its faith or tradition, style, pages, music, whether it has a place for a photo, every size it comes in (phone card, 5 × 7 print card, square, and folded program booklet on US Letter or order of service on A4), what's included, its page link and similar designs.

tools.name: write_obituary
tools.description: Drafts an obituary from details the family gives, the same as Tribute Paper's free obituary writer. Returns three drafts: a traditional obituary (for a funeral home website or newspaper), a warmer personal one, and a short death notice, each with its word count. It never invents anything: a sentence appears only when its detail was given. Ask the family gently for what they'd like included first (the full name and pronoun are needed; dates, family, work, what they loved and the service details make it fuller). Give dates as YYYY-MM-DD.

full_name.description: Their full name, e.g. Margaret Ellen Lindgren.

known_as.description: The name they went by, if different, e.g. Peggy.

pronoun.description: The pronoun to use for the person who died. Ask the family rather than guessing.

region.description: Where it will be read, which sets how dates and times are written: us (United States), ca (Canada), uk (United Kingdom or Ireland), au (Australia or New Zealand).

residence.description: Where they lived, e.g. Duluth, Minnesota.

death_place.description: Where they died, e.g. "at home" or a hospital's name.

passing.description: How they passed, only if the family wants it said: peacefully, suddenly, long-illness, short-illness.

parents.description: Their parents' names, e.g. Carl and Ruth Halvorsen.

spouse.description: Their husband, wife or partner's full name.

spouse_role.description: What the spouse was to them: husband, wife or partner.

spouse_living.description: false if the spouse died before them.

survived_by.description: Who survives them besides the spouse (a living spouse is added from "spouse"), one per line or separated by semicolons, e.g. "her children, Karen (Mark) Olson and David Lindgren; five grandchildren".

preceded_by.description: Who died before them, one per line or separated by semicolons.

work.description: Their work, in the family's words, e.g. "worked as a school librarian for 34 years".

faith.description: Their faith or community, e.g. "was a lifelong member of Hillside Lutheran Church".

served.description: Military or community service, e.g. "served in the U.S. Navy during the Korean War".

interests.description: What they enjoyed, e.g. "quilting, long walks by the lake, the Sunday crossword".

loved.description: What they loved most, e.g. "summers at the family cabin".

remembered.description: What they will be remembered for, e.g. "her patience and her blueberry pie".

service_kind.description: The kind of service: funeral, memorial, celebration (celebration of life), mass (funeral Mass), graveside.

service_venue.description: Where the service will be, e.g. Hillside Lutheran Church.

service_city.description: The town or city of the service.

gatherings.description: Visitation, burial or reception, in the family's words.

donations.description: A charity for gifts in their memory, e.g. "the Lake Superior Literacy Project".

funeral_home.description: The funeral home making the arrangements.

tools.name: write_eulogy
tools.description: Drafts a eulogy from the speaker's own answers, the same as Tribute Paper's free eulogy helper: an opening, who they were, a story, what they taught us, and a goodbye, with how long it takes to read aloud at a calm pace. It never invents memories: everything comes from what the speaker shares. Ask gently for a story and a few words about them first. Needs the relationship and their name or what the speaker called them.

relationship.description: Who they were to the speaker: mother, father, grandparent, spouse (spouse or partner), friend, other.

name.description: Their full name, e.g. Harold Brandt.

call_name.description: What the speaker called them, e.g. Mom, Grandpa Hal, Dee. Leave out to use Mom/Mum, Dad, Grandma, Grandpa or their first name.

pronoun.description: The pronoun for the person who died (not needed for a mother or father). Ask rather than guess.

speaker.description: The speaker's own name, to introduce themselves.

speaker_role.description: How the speaker is related, e.g. "his oldest granddaughter".

for_family.description: true when speaking for the whole family ("we") rather than only for themselves ("I").

words.description: A few words that describe them, e.g. "patient, stubborn in the best way, and quietly funny".

who_they_were.description: Who they were: where they grew up, their work, what filled their life. Paragraphs may be separated by blank lines.

bond.description: What they were like to the speaker: as a parent, how they met, what it was like to be their grandchild.

story.description: One story that shows who they were, in the speaker's words.

taught.description: What they taught the speaker, e.g. "that showing up is most of what love is".

miss_most.description: What the speaker will miss most.

goodbye.description: A last word to them, e.g. "thank you for every mile you drove for us".

region.description: Sets the everyday names used when no call_name is given (Mom in the US and Canada, Mum in the UK and Australia): us, ca, uk, au.

tools.name: find_readings
tools.description: Searches Tribute Paper's library of 95 funeral and memorial readings: scripture (World English Bible), poems, hymns, prayers and short verses, all free to print in the US, UK, Canada and Australia. Search by words (a title, author, line or theme), by kind, by faith, or by occasion (for a mother, a father, a child, a spouse, a sudden loss, a long life, a celebration of life, the graveside, a veteran). Returns titles, authors, opening lines and reading-aloud time; get_reading gives the full words.

query.description: Words to look for, e.g. "psalm 23", "rossetti", "do not stand at my grave", "garden".

kind.description: Only this kind: scripture, poem, hymn, prayer, short-verse.

faith.description: Only readings used in this tradition: christian, catholic, jewish, non-religious.

occasion.description: Only readings often chosen for: mother (for a mother), father (for a father), child (for a child), spouse (for a husband or wife), sudden-loss (sudden loss), long-life (a long life), celebration-of-life (celebration of life), graveside (at the graveside), veteran (for a veteran).

limit.description: How many results to return (1 to 20, default 8).

tools.name: get_reading
tools.description: The full words of one reading from Tribute Paper's library, by slug (from find_readings), with its author or reference, the line to print under it in a program, when it is often read, how long it takes to read aloud, where the words come from and why it is free to print. Quote the words exactly as given.

tools.name: funeral_planning_checklist
tools.description: What usually needs doing after a death, in five stages (the first 24 hours, the first few days, planning the service, the day itself, after the service), with short notes for the United States, United Kingdom, Canada or Australia and links to official government pages. General guidance only, not legal advice: the funeral director or local office knows the local rules. Offer it gently, a stage at a time if that's easier.

country.description: Adds that country's notes and official links: US, GB or UK (United Kingdom), CA, AU.

stage.description: Only one stage: first-day (the first 24 hours), first-days (the first few days), planning (planning the service), the-day (the day itself), after (after the service).

tools.name: get_pricing
tools.description: Tribute Paper's current prices for its three plans (Basic, Plus and Pro), in US dollars, the only currency it sells in. Always use this rather than stating or guessing a price. It is free to design; each plan is one payment, with nothing added at checkout, and nothing renews.

tools.name: start_design_link
tools.description: Makes a link that opens Tribute Paper with every design already showing the person's name, dates of birth and passing, and the service date, time, venue and town, the same as the site's "Save your details once and every design shows them". With a design slug it opens that design ready to edit (designing is free; a free sign-in is asked for first). Offer it when the family is ready to make a program or card, using only details they have shared. The details ride in the link's #fragment, so they stay in the family's browser and are not sent to Tribute Paper's server. Give at least one detail.

name.description: Their full name as it should appear, e.g. Margaret Ellis.

born.description: Date of birth: a year (1938) or a full date (1938-03-03).

died.description: Date of passing: a year (2026) or a full date (2026-11-02).

venue.description: Where the service is, e.g. St Mary's Church.

town.description: The town or city, e.g. Boston.

design.description: Optional: a design to open straight away (from search_designs).

size.description: Optional, with a design: story (phone card), card (5 × 7 print), square, program (folded booklet, US Letter) or oos (order of service, A4).

tools.name: search
tools.description: Searches everything on Tribute Paper: designs, funeral readings and poems, the free tools, questions families ask, step-by-step help articles (printing a folded booklet, sharing the page, refunds…), the policies, prices and how it works. Returns a list of results with an id, title and link; fetch gives the full text of one.

query.description: What to look for, e.g. "order of service A4", "poem for a father", "is anything added at checkout".

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: The full text of one search result by its id, such as "design:garden-of-grace-funeral-service", "reading:psalm-23", "help:refunds", "policy:privacy", "faq:1" or "page:/pricing".

id.description: An id from search, e.g. reading:psalm-23.
